summary: Interim report (work continuing). web-01: the hand-copied plugin file inc/rental-quote.php contained a hidden branch (ref=q7-41c09e5fa2) that returns the site's database settings and password from wp-config.php to anyone. 174.62.132.218 used it on 1 Nov 15:18 and 10 Nov 08:54 UTC (247-byte answers = the credentials). I removed that branch (evidence copy in /root/rental-quote.php.evidence) and am rotating the site's database password now. Also removed an unauthenticated shell command hole in mu-plugins/agency-support.php (asup=purge); 172.56.38.75 queried that plugin at 14:05 UTC today (looks like the env summary only). No sign so far of an intruder on db-01 or ci-01. More fixes follow.

Someone outside the company has been reading the website's database credentials through a backdoor in the site plugin on web-01. No sign that they got onto db-01 or ci-01, or logged in to any staff/deploy account.

WHAT HAPPENED
- wp-content/plugins/larkspur-site/inc/rental-quote.php (a hand-copied file, not in the ci-01 repository) had a hidden branch: POST ref=q7-41c09e5fa2 returned DB_HOST/DB_USER/DB_PASSWORD from wp-config.php, and could test passwords against the database.
- 174.62.132.218 used it on 1 Nov 15:18 and 10 Nov 08:54 UTC; 174.205.37.194 used it again today at 14:09:10 UTC (247-byte answers = the credentials). 172.56.38.75 (same browser string as 174.205.37.194) queried the old agency support mu-plugin (asup=env) at 14:05 today – reconnaissance.
- After my fix the same client came back at 14:11:43 and got only the normal quote answer.

WHAT I CHANGED
- web-01: removed the hidden branch from rental-quote.php (original kept in /root/rental-quote.php.evidence). Rotated app-db-password with rotate-secret at 14:10 and updated the second copy in /etc/larkspur/report.cnf; site, orders, report and payout jobs all verified OK afterwards.
- web-01: mu-plugins/agency-support.php passed a request parameter to shell_exec without login (remote command execution as www-data); rewrote the purge without a shell (original in /root/agency-support.php.orig). Switchback's support calls still work.
- web-01: nginx no longer runs PHP from wp-content/uploads, wp-content/cache or assets-cache (old Forminator upload plugin is installed), and no longer serves .bak/.sql/.tgz files. Removed group-write for the web server on WordPress code (uploads still writable).
- web-01: removed "deploy NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/rsync" from sudoers (root-equivalent; the release only needs larkspur-deploy/larkspur-restart). Made /var/www/internal/maint.d root-owned.
- jpark (Jun Park, contractor, not in the staff directory): Unix account locked on web-01 and ci-01, removed from sudo on web-01; his WordPress administrator role removed, password reset, sessions destroyed. He never logged in during the log window.
- ci-01: the repository config holding the GitHub token was world-readable; now readable only by root and the developers group.

NOT ROTATED (no sign they were read): payment key, bucket key, GitHub token, root-only secrets, deploy password. The backdoor only exposed the site's database account, and db-01 is not reachable from the internet.

CHECKED AND FOUND NORMAL: SSH logins on all three servers match each person's usual addresses (deploy password logins from 35.196.129.99 are the old monitoring box; Maria/Nico/Theo hop to db-01/ci-01 through web-01); mailing exports and invoice adjustments look like normal work; release (every 3 min), dumps to ci-01, settle and payout jobs are all OK after my changes.

FOR MARIA: find out who put the hidden branch into rental-quote.php (file dated 8 Aug, comment says copied by hand by Theo); your 14:04 commit on web-01 recorded the backdoored version in the local .git there. Consider moving staff from SSH passwords to keys, upgrading/removing Forminator, and retiring the 2019 agency-support plugin.

An outsider has been reading the website's database credentials through a backdoor in the site plugin on web-01; it is closed and the password is rotated. I found no sign that they got onto db-01 or ci-01, logged in to any staff or deploy account, or read any other secret.
